summary: CORRECTION + ESCALATION. Docker Desktop's Linux VM hard-failed at 2026-08-25T05:47:39Z with 'FATAL: running services: running fs: injecting event blocked for 60s' — dockerd stopped, hypervisor process stopped, ALL containers down. Every docker CLI call now returns 'Docker Desktop is unable to start'. This SUPERSEDES the root-cause attribution in dev-team-20260825T054306Z.json, which blamed an app-level blocked event loop in mcp-server. The mcp-server silence from 05:16:16Z was almost certainly the FIRST symptom of this same VM filesystem-sharing layer degrading, not an independent app bug.

payload.what_changed: That signal attributed the mcp-server wedge to an app-level event-loop block after a write-visibility error, with root cause UNCONFIRMED. Host-side Docker logs now show the failure is one layer down: the VM's filesystem event-injection service. The write-invisibility symptom (count=107, visible_now=0 at 05:16Z) is consistent with the fs-sharing layer failing to propagate writes, which is exactly the subsystem that later hard-blocked. Treat the mcp-server wedge as a DOWNSTREAM EFFECT, not the fault.

evidence.vm_init_log_fatal: log source: ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/log/vm/init.log — {"component":"init","level":"error","msg":"FATAL: running services: running fs: injecting event blocked for 60s","time":"2026-08-25T05:47:39.421665222Z"}
evidence.dockerd_stop: {"component":"init","msg":"dockerd exited due to explicit Stop() call","time":"2026-08-25T05:47:39.191400102Z"} — dockerd stopped ~230ms BEFORE the FATAL line was emitted
evidence.pause_resume: initd /pause/events shows 'pause resuming' -> 'pause resumed: Docker Desktop is running' at 05:47:38.78Z, i.e. ~600ms BEFORE dockerd was stopped. A resume immediately preceding the fs FATAL is the strongest single lead.
evidence.broken_pipe: apiproxy: 'forwarding raw stream to dockerd: ... write unix @->/var/run/docker.raw.sock: write: broken pipe' plus a burst of 'closing response body: unexpected EOF' at 05:47:39.11Z
evidence.current_cli_state: docker version / docker ps / docker info all return 'Error response from daemon: Docker Desktop is unable to start'; docker info reports containers=0 running=0
evidence.backend_ipc_now: com.docker.backend.ipc GET /ping -> 'context deadline exceeded' on a 10s cadence, continuously, as of 2026-08-25T05:52:05Z
evidence.endpoints: localhost:3000/health http=000 (8s timeout); localhost:3001/ http=000 (8s timeout) — frontend, which had briefly recovered at 05:43Z, is now down too

differential_diagnosis.NOT_hypervisor_crash: No ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/hypervisor.error.json exists, and /Users/admin/.docker/run/docker.sock IS present. This is NOT the 2026-07-15 signature (that one had the socket ABSENT plus a hypervisor.error.json virtualization error). Do NOT jump to that incident's exhausted recovery ladder.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_host_sleep: pmset -g log for 2026-08-25 shows no Sleep/Wake/DarkWake transitions across the incident window — only caffeinate assertions actively PREVENTING idle sleep. Host suspension is ruled out.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_process_restart: com.docker.backend (pid 14371) and Docker Desktop (pid 23968) both have lstart of 15 jul 2026 — the Docker Desktop processes have NOT restarted. The backend is alive (18.9% CPU) but its VM is gone.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_OOM: Last successful inspect of mcp-server-1 showed 508MiB/3GiB, RestartCount=0, CPU 0.18%.

asks: Diagnose the fs event-injection block — this is the virtiofs/osxfs file-sharing layer. Check which bind-mount was being watched when it blocked; the repo bind-mount (./docs/data, ./data/pdfs) is the prime suspect given the fleet writes those paths constantly.

Recover the daemon. Because the socket exists and no hypervisor error was written, a normal Docker Desktop restart is the FIRST thing to try and is likely sufficient. Escalate to the user only if that fails.

CRITICAL SAFETY CONSTRAINT — do NOT under any circumstances 'rebuild the VM from scratch' (i.e. remove ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms) as a recovery step. On Docker Desktop/Mac, named volumes live INSIDE the VM disk image; that step DESTROYED market_data and bctc-page-images on 2026-07-15 and required a 361MB backup restore. If the daemon does return, verify market_data volume integrity (row counts + MAX(date)) BEFORE trusting green health.

Investigate whether Docker Desktop's Resource Saver / pause feature is enabled. A pause->resume transition ~600ms before the fs FATAL suggests resume-from-pause is the trigger. If so, disabling Resource Saver is a candidate permanent fix for a recurring outage class.

Re-check whether the mcp-server write-invisibility symptom (count=107, visible_now=0) still reproduces once the daemon is healthy. If it does NOT, that confirms it was fs-layer collateral and the earlier app-level bug hypothesis can be closed.

probe_defect_found.what: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh mem_creep check misclassifies 'stats-unavailable' as a memory-threshold breach.
probe_defect_found.detail: This tick's verdict reports mem_creep FAIL with detail 'mem >= 85% threshold (A-30 WARN boundary, mem-creep gate)' listing all 10 containers as '(stats-unavailable)'. docker stats returning nothing because the daemon is DEAD is not memory creep — it is the absence of a reading. Reporting absence-of-data as a threshold breach is a false positive of exactly the class that erodes trust in the probe.
probe_defect_found.downstream_harm: The emitted signature is 'health_3000|mem_creep:<all 10 container names>'. That bogus 10-container signature is now written into docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json (spawn_count=1, window_expires_at 2026-08-25T06:47:51Z). A genuine future single-container mem_creep will produce a DIFFERENT signature and will therefore not dedup against it — the debounce ledger has been polluted with an unrepeatable key.
probe_defect_found.fix: Treat stats-unavailable as a distinct third state (UNKNOWN/SKIP), never as FAIL. When the daemon itself is unreachable, mem_creep should be reported as not-evaluated and docker_ps should be the failing check.

second_probe_defect.what: docker_ps scored PASS in the same tick where the docker daemon is unreachable.
second_probe_defect.detail: The 05:47:51Z verdict records checks.docker_ps=PASS alongside health_3000=FAIL. Roughly 10 seconds later every docker CLI invocation returns 'Docker Desktop is unable to start'. Either docker_ps ran before the 05:47:50Z hypervisor stop (a genuine race, in which case it is merely stale), or its success predicate does not actually require a daemon response. Worth confirming which, because a docker_ps that can PASS with no daemon is a blind spot in the single most important check the probe has.
second_probe_defect.note: Timing makes the benign race plausible here — the probe wrote at 05:47:51Z and the hypervisor stopped at 05:47:50.55Z. Flagged for confirmation rather than asserted as a defect.

fleet_impact.all_mcp_tools: Every call_tool(server=vn-market, ...) is unreachable. All lock gates (task_claim / task_heartbeat / task_release) are down fleet-wide.
fleet_impact.dev_team_ticks: The 05:37Z tick already failed to dispatch on an unreachable SF-1 gate. Every subsequent 7,37 tick will hit the same wall until the daemon returns.
fleet_impact.auditor_t1: This tick (fire_tick 2026-08-25T05:30Z, written 05:47:51Z) correctly returned verdict=FAILURE with spawn_decision=SPAWN. The router did NOT spawn system-auditor: its flow's own fire-election task_claim gate (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md, EXIT on non-claim) is structurally unreachable with the daemon down, so a compliant auditor would exit at its first gate before doing any tier work. Detection already succeeded; escalation is this file.
fleet_impact.unreleased_lock: task:TASK-DEV-MCP-SIGNAL-TYPE-REGISTRY remains held by session 036ceaf1-bf34-46cd-92e4-8c6b213ff4bb (task_release timed out 3x earlier). TTL 3600s bounds it and the row is terminal (DONE_VERIFIED), so it self-expires harmlessly. All fleet locks will now expire naturally while the daemon is down.
fleet_impact.publishing: Any scheduled chef/fb-poster/market-watcher cycle firing during the outage will find every data tool unreachable.

router_actions_taken: Did NOT spawn system-auditor — its mandatory fire-election gate is unreachable (see fleet_impact.auditor_t1). Reasoning recorded rather than silently skipped.
Diagnosed the outage from host-side Docker logs only (no container action, no daemon restart attempted — recovery is ops scope).
Took NO recovery action: did not restart Docker Desktop, did not kill any Docker process, did not touch the VM data directory.
Filed this corrected escalation superseding the root-cause attribution in dev-team-20260825T054306Z.json.

post_filing_update.headline: A clean Docker Desktop relaunch was attempted and FAILED to bootstrap the VM. Ask #2 of this signal ("a normal restart is the FIRST thing to try and is likely sufficient") is now empirically FALSIFIED — do not spend a cycle on it.

evidence.relaunch: com.docker.backend.log 2026-08-25T06:00:41Z — onApplicationDidFinishLaunching, auth.enforcer "unholding Engines, they will start now". Backend pids changed from 14369/14371/14372 to 5809/5827/5828, confirming a genuine process relaunch (not a reconnect).
evidence.vm_never_started: vm/init.log has NOT advanced a single line past the 05:47:39.421Z FATAL in the 7+ minutes since the relaunch. The VM is not booting at all — this is not a slow bootstrap.
evidence.backend_idle: After 06:00:41Z the backend log contains only analytics traffic (06:05:39Z marlin batch). No engine-start progress of any kind.
evidence.cli_surface_changed: docker CLI error moved from "Docker Desktop is unable to start" (backend answering, refusing) to "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///Users/admin/.docker/run/docker.sock" (nothing listening). The socket FILE is still present; no process is bound to it.
evidence.still_not_hypervisor_signature: hypervisor.error.json is STILL absent, so this remains distinct from the 2026-07-15 incident despite the relaunch failure.

post_filing_update.revised_recommendation: Escalate toward host-level action sooner than this signal originally implied. The remaining bounded CLI step is the comprehensive teardown-to-zero (killall -9 Docker "Docker Desktop" com.docker.backend com.docker.build com.docker.dev-envs vpnkit; pkill -9 -i docker) followed by one clean `open -a Docker` — worth EXACTLY ONE attempt. If the socket still does not bootstrap after that, STOP and escalate to the user for GUI recovery / reboot. Do NOT re-run the ladder repeatedly; that failure mode is already documented.
post_filing_update.constraint_reaffirmed: The do-NOT-rebuild-the-VM constraint in asks[2] is UNCHANGED and becomes MORE important as pressure to escalate rises. Removing ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms destroys every named volume including market_data.
